body:
Current requirements:
| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **7.4.2** | [MODIFIED] Verify that a consistent and standardized exception handling mechanism (or a functional equivalent) is used across the codebase. | 2 | 544 |
| **7.4.3** | Verify that a "last resort" error handler is defined which will catch all unhandled exceptions. | 2 | 431 |

What precise security problem 7.4.2 solves or we can define this as code-beauty? I think it is "imported" from CWE definition.

If 7.4.2 is not covered by 7.4.3, I recommend to have 7.4.2 as Level 3 requirement.

... or, did I miss something?

comments.body: Proper exception handling typically addresses security problems such as information leakage and system stability resulting from error states. It’s typically a lot more than code beauty. Poor exception handling leaks data about system internals and makes software significantly more unstable.

Leaking sensitive data is covered by 7.4.1 (currently under discussion in #2628).

The question is - what does 7.4.2 give from a security perspective, that is not covered by 7.4.1 and 7.4.3? Taking into account, it must be verifiable.
I would overall say no and agree with you that it can go. Any arguments to keep it around would be weak, in my opinion.

To be more clear with proposal - I don't see any unique aspect of security from requirement 7.4.2 and propose to delete it as `DELETED, INSUFFICIENT IMPACT`

ping @tghosth
